How is Knit structured for offline high-performance desktop processing?

Long image

A

Answer

Knit isolates heavy domain logic into six pure-Rust crates decoupled from GUI frameworks, bridged by a thin Tauri v2 desktop adapter to a responsive React workbench.

  1. Pure Rust core crates (crates/knit-*) run 100% offline with zero GUI dependencies, ensuring complete testability via cargo test.
  2. Thin desktop shell (src-tauri) manages OS dialogs, background worker pools, and throttled IPC progress events.
  3. React frontend handles interactive drag-and-drop, normalized canvas editing, and virtualized thumbnail grids without holding heavy bitmaps in memory.
  4. Non-destructive PageDraft pipeline and atomic file outputs protect source files and eliminate partial or corrupted disk writes.

Applies toKnit v1.0Desktop architectureRust + Tauri v2 + React

How does the async job lifecycle prevent UI freezing?

Diagram structure
  • User user
  • React UI ui
  • Tauri IPC ipc
  • Rayon Pool pool
  • Local Disk fs
  • user → ui · Trigger Export / Batch Job
  • ui → ipc · invoke("start_job", config)
  • ipc → pool · spawn background worker
  • ipc → ui · return JobId immediately
  • pool → fs · verify disk space & stream inputs
  • pool → fs · write atomic temp file (.tmp/.part)
  • pool → ipc · emit JobProgress (~10Hz throttled)
  • ipc → ui · update progress bar & logs
  • pool → fs · atomic rename (.tmp -> final.pdf)
  • pool → ipc · emit JobCompleted
  • ipc → ui · show success toast & free heap
